correctness.rationale: The determinant AM-GM argument proves the global maximizer and exact equality orbit; trace-free matrix coordinates provide a complete orthogonal quotient by rotations. Differentiating augmented determinant along spherical geodesics yields the Hessian forms, diagonalized algebraically into dimensions d and (d+1)(d-2)/2 with eigenvalues 1 and 2d/(d+1) after normalization. The orbit is compact, so the standard tubular neighborhood Taylor expansion gives sharp distance coefficients; a standalone numerical verifier checks d=2..6 and 30 finite-difference geodesics. Finite checks are not treated as proof.

value.rationale: Prescribed-radius maximum-volume simplices are canonical extremizers. Their full intrinsic Hessian and sharp distance stability distinguish d soft vertex motions from (d+1)(d-2)/2 stiffer deformations. Identifying the exact nonzero spectrum and absence of further flat modes gives substantive all-dimensional shape rigidity beyond known maximum/equality statements or random-volume laws; no external major theorem is necessary for validity.
